inputs.share_count_basis: 550.6m diluted weighted-average common shares (Q2 FY2027 10-Q, treasury-method RSUs included) plus 23.8m shares from the 7.50% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred on an if-converted basis (1.485m preferred x 16.006 minimum rate; the 10-Q's own anti-dilution exclusion figure). The preferred converts automatically on 2028-03-15, so it is equity, not debt. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The 2024 and 2026 convertible notes (conversion prices 121.79 and 104.17) are out of the money and carried at principal in debt; the 2017 notes are 37.9m principal.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation add-back 255.4 plus 51.4 tax payments on shares withheld for vested RSUs (financing). Microchip publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed per the house rule.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate. Risk-free ~4.25% (10-year UST), ERP 5.0%, equity beta ~1.4 for a levered analog/MCU cyclical gives cost of equity ~11.2%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.5% at roughly 14% debt weight gives ~10.2%, rounded to 10.0% (house USD reference 10.5%). One WACC across all three scenarios: cyclicality and leverage are priced in the flows and the weights, not stacked in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (145.8m liability at FY2026) are already expensed inside operating costs and therefore inside EBITDA; lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. One treatment, no separate lease line.
inputs.interest_income_treatment: Not stripped: the company carries net DEBT of 5.1bn, interest income was 11.4m in FY2026, and the component build is unlevered (EBITDA-based) so neither interest income nor interest expense is in the projected flows.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon, with the cyclical adaptations (risk charged once, negative working-capital capture, lower terminal cap). Chosen because Microchip is an operating semiconductor company whose value is its free cash flow; none of the bank/REIT/NAV routes apply. First valuation of this ticker. CYCLE POSITION: FY0 (FY2026, March year-end) is a trough year - revenue 4,713 against the FY2023 peak of 8,439, pre-SBC EBITDA margin 30% against 51% at peak - so last_fcf of 564 is NOT the base the projection grows from; the component build re-derives every year. H1 FY2027 revenue was 3,106 (+40% y/y) with Q2 at 1,621.5, GAAP gross margin 65.9%, and TTM reported FCF of about 1,455. Year 1 (FY2027) is therefore anchored to H1 actuals plus a flat-to-slightly-up H2; no December-quarter guidance was available in the 10-Q text. The FY2023 peak is treated as an over-shipment year (distributor inventory then rebuilt from 24 to 43 days) and is not regained in the base case until FY2032. Mature pre-SBC EBITDA margin of 44% sits between the 7-year average (~41%, FY2020-FY2026) and the FY2022-FY2024 range (47-51%). Capex path includes 'investments in other assets' (110.8m FY2026, 114.7m in H1 FY2027) which the company's own FCF definition omits. BUYBACKS: none since FY2025 (96.5m); the flat share count is currently a modelling convention the company is not funding - cash is going to the 0.455/quarter common dividend (~990m/yr) which exceeded FY2026 FCF. NOT IN THE BRIDGE: long-term income tax payable of 592.8m (uncertain tax positions; transition tax fully paid by March 2026) and deferred tax assets of 1,821m; they roughly offset in sign and the below-statutory cash tax path carries the DTA benefit. Q2 FY2027 net income included a discrete deferred-tax benefit from legal-entity restructuring, so the 10.8% H1 effective rate is not a run-rate. No Analysis JSON existed for this ticker at build time; scenario axes come from the 10-K/10-Q MD&A.

equity_bridge.item: Series A preferred dividends remaining to mandatory conversion
equity_bridge.note: 27.8m per quarter, six payments Dec-2026 to Mar-2028 (167m undiscounted); the preferred itself is in the share count on an if-converted basis

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR diverges by far more than 30% from revenue and EPS CAGRs. Every trailing CAGR ends on the FY2026 trough (and the 3-year ones start on the FY2023 peak), so none is a usable growth anchor; the forward path is built from H1 FY2027 actuals and a mid-cycle view instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series = OCF - capex - SBC add-back - RSU withholding taxes: FY2021 1,561.0, FY2023 2,888.6, FY2026 564.2. Owner FCF fell faster than reported FCF (-42% vs -35% 3-year) because SBC rose from 170m to 255m while revenue nearly halved - SBC plus withholding taxes went from 2.9% of revenue in FY2023 to 6.5% in FY2026.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-SBC EBITDA (operating income + D&A + SBC). H1 FY2027 actual 40.6%, Q2 ~42.7%; FY2023 peak 50.8%; FY2020-FY2026 average ~41%.
base.da_note: Includes acquired-intangible amortisation (~360m/yr, 1.9bn remaining, rolling off) which is why the path falls toward depreciation-only levels.
base.capex_note: PP&E capex (guided at or below 100m for the next 12 months, normalising to ~4% of revenue as the expansion pause ends) plus ~1.5% of revenue of investments in other assets.
base.wc_note: Manufacturer: receivables plus inventory less payables is ~28% of run-rate revenue, but inventory at 184 days is still above target, so incremental growth consumes less than the average.

scenario_narratives.base: The inventory correction is over - distributor inventory is back to 25 days from a 43-day peak, every product line and geography grew sequentially in the September 2026 quarter, and a price increase has gone through. FY2027 lands near 6.4bn (+36%) on H1 actuals plus a flat-to-up second half. From there revenue grows at mid-single digits as a through-cycle average and does not regain the FY2023 over-shipment peak of 8.4bn until FY2032. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin settles at 44%: above today's 41-43% as underutilisation charges and inventory reserves finish unwinding after the Fab 2 closure, but short of the 47-51% of FY2022-FY2024, which were earned on allocation-era pricing and full factories. SBC plus withholding taxes drifts from ~6% of revenue back to 4% as revenue rebuilds; capex normalises to 5.5% including other-asset investments once the expansion pause ends.
scenario_narratives.bull: The recovery turns into a proper upcycle: data-centre, aerospace-and-defence and FPGA demand plus design wins entering production carry FY2028 revenue to ~7.5bn and the FY2023 peak is passed by FY2030. Price increases hold, licensing revenue stays elevated, and with Fab 2 closed and headcount resized the fixed-cost base is smaller than last cycle, so pre-SBC EBITDA margin returns to 48% - still below the 50.8% peak. This needs both pricing discipline across MCU/analog peers and no repeat of the customer over-ordering that produced the 2023-2025 bust.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2027's rebound proves to be partly restocking and price-driven. Tariffs and a recession hit industrial and automotive demand in FY2028-FY2029 (revenue -8%, -6%), Chinese MCU and analog suppliers take share in the 48%-of-sales Asia region and force the recent price increases to be handed back, and 184 days of balance-sheet inventory brings underutilisation charges back. Margin troughs at 35% and recovers only to 39%. With 5.1bn of net debt, 2.15bn of convertible notes to refinance in 2027-2029 and a ~990m common dividend, there is no room for buybacks and SBC stays near 5% of a smaller revenue base.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default: another semiconductor downcycle inside a 10-year horizon is close to certain, the last one took revenue down 48% peak-to-trough, and the company carries 5.1bn of net debt with a dividend that exceeded trough FCF. Base 50%: a mid-cycle path anchored to H1 FY2027 actuals. Bull cut to 25% from 35%: it needs pricing to hold, share to hold in Asia, and margins to return within 3 points of an allocation-era peak - several independent things.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Valued on mid-cycle owner free cash flow, not on the FY2026 trough and not on the FY2023 peak. SBC and RSU withholding taxes are expensed in full and the share count (including the mandatory convertible preferred as-converted) is held flat. The flows are unlevered; 5.1bn of net debt and the remaining preferred dividends come off enterprise value. Cyclicality is carried by the scenario paths and the 25% bear weight rather than by a WACC premium.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cycle timing: year-1 is anchored to a quarter that included a price increase and a licensing spike (71m vs ~33m typical); if H2 FY2027 rolls over the whole path shifts down
Mature margin: each point of terminal pre-SBC EBITDA margin is worth roughly 1.5 dollars per share in the base case (estimate, not an engine output)
Leverage: 5.55bn gross debt against 457m cash; 1.25bn and 0.9bn convertibles and 3bn of 2028-2030 notes need refinancing at higher coupons than the 0-0.75% converts carry
SBC has risen to 5-6% of revenue with no buybacks offsetting it since FY2025; the flat-count convention is unfunded while the dividend absorbs free cash flow
Capex is being held at a paused level (at or below 100m); the model assumes it more than doubles as a share of revenue, and a faster catch-up would cut near-term FCF

Discount rate: the valuation is at a 10% WACC; the base path is worth less than the market price even at a 9% required return (see required_return_table), so the price is paying for a better path than base or a lower rate
